site_name: QTS Glendale campus (QTS PHX3), 17501 W Bethany Home Rd
notes: Utility: APS's own 2024 annual progress report to WECC describes the Dromedary 230kV switchyard 'at the northwest corner of Camelback Road and Cotton Lane in Glendale', built 'to provide electric energy to a new high-load customer'. The report does not name the customer; the match to QTS rests on location (trade press places the QTS campus north of Camelback Rd along Cotton Lane, west of Loop 303), hence medium not high. None of the irrigation/electrical districts on the candidate list appears in any source. Contract form (tariff vs special contract) not found. Year: APS lists the Dromedary 230kV lines with a 2025 in-service date (2024 and 2026 reports); that is the utility interconnection, NOT confirmed commercial operation of the first building, so 2025 is low confidence. No operator statement of an opening date was found; 2023-2024 trade press still described the campus as planned. Load: no public operating-load or built-capacity figure for 2025; the 405 MW in-house estimate is unverified. Planned build-out: 'more than 750 MW of critical power', 16 buildings, 29-acre substation (https://commercialsearch.com/news/qts-eyes-3rd-phoenix-data-center-campus, May 2024). A directory site also lists APS as provider (lead only, not cited).

site_name: Google Omaha data center (northwest Omaha, State St and Blair High Rd)
notes: Utility: Nebraska Examiner reporting (republished by KMTV) on the site plan says 'A security entrance and Omaha Public Power District switchyard are to be on site'; OPPD is also the only mapped utility. No special-contract filing was looked up, so 'retail' means OPPD is the retail supplier, contract form not verified. Year: Flatwater Free Press (13 Mar 2026): announced 2022, 'The data center started operating in 2024 even as construction on the site continued.' Single news source, so medium. Load: no public MW figure for this campus was found; the 237 MW in-house estimate is unverified. Site grew from about 260 to more than 450 acres per the same reporting; no planned MW published.

site_name: Apple Maiden data center, 5977 Startown Rd
load_basis: Average load implied by Apple-reported electricity use at Maiden of 466 million kWh in 2024 (466 GWh / 8,784 h = 53.1 MW average). Latest published year is 2024, not 2025; peak load and IT capacity are not published.
notes: Apple's 2025 Environmental Progress Report (data center appendix): Maiden '100 percent renewable since opening June 2010'; refers to 'the local utility, Duke Energy' and Duke's Green Source Rider projects; 'Electricity use in 2024: 466 million kWh' (453 million kWh in 2023 per the 2024 report). The 2022 generator permit is an expansion, not the first building; our 2023 guess is wrong. Apple also built 68 MW of its own solar and biogas fuel-cell projects near the site between 2011 and 2015; the report does not say how much, if any, of that is behind the meter, so net utility deliveries could be lower than 53 MW. Rutherford EMC appears in no source. No planned build-out MW published.

site_name: Digital Realty Building L (Digital Loudoun III campus), 44274 Round Table Plaza
serving_utility: Virginia Electric & Power Co (Dominion Energy Virginia)
load_basis: Design IT capacity of Building L phase 1 (six data halls of 6 MW each) per Sept 2017 trade press. Treat as a floor: two later phases were planned to take the building to 84 MW and their status by 2025 was not confirmed.
notes: Utility: no building-specific utility document found. Bisnow (29 Jul 2022) reports Dominion Energy as the utility for Ashburn data centers and quotes Digital Realty on its Dominion relationship and substations already built at its facilities; Dominion is also the only mapped utility. Medium because the source is not specific to this building. Year: Data Center Frontier (15 Sep 2017): 'The first data hall in Building L is partially leased, and scheduled to be delivered on October 1', second hall in December. That is a scheduled date two weeks out, not a confirmed one; it is earlier than our 2019 guess from the 2018 generator permit. Planned: 84 MW is for this building; the whole Digital Loudoun III campus was planned at 324 MW of IT capacity across eight buildings (same article). A directory site lists a larger commissioned figure for this building (lead only, not cited).

site_name: Galaxy Helios campus (CoreWeave tenant), Dickens County
serving_utility: Wind Energy Transmission Texas, LLC (WETT) - transmission-level interconnection only; no retail delivery utility identified
notes: Utility NOT established. The only named provider found is in a vendor blog (Introl, 7 Feb 2026): 'Wind Energy Transmission Texas (WETT) provides interconnection.' WETT is a transmission-only utility, so this does not identify a retail delivery utility, and no Galaxy, CoreWeave, ERCOT, PUCT or co-op document was found (SEC full-text search and several trade sites refused automated access; Galaxy's own Helios page names no provider). No source ties South Plains EC, Lighthouse EC or AEP Texas North to the site, so our South Plains guess is unsupported; matches_ours=false reflects that, at low confidence. Year: Data Center Knowledge (28 Jul 2026) reports Helios 'had delivered roughly 200 MW of gross power, including 133 MW of critical IT load' to CoreWeave earlier that month, so the AI data center entered service in 2026. The SITE was first energized in May 2022 as Argo Blockchain's bitcoin mine (https://www.theblock.co/post/145257/argos-texas-flagship-facility-has-been-energized; planned 200 MW by end of 2022) and sold to Galaxy in Dec 2022; use 2022 if the question is when large load first appeared at this interconnection. Load 2025: null because the CoreWeave halls were not yet delivered in 2025 and no 2025 mining-load figure was found; by July 2026 the figure is 133 MW critical IT (about 200 MW gross). Planned: 800 MW is the approved gross power fully committed to CoreWeave (https://convergedigest.com/coreweave-locks-in-800-mw-at-galaxys-helios-campus-in-texas/); Galaxy's site lists total approved campus capacity of 1.6+ GW (https://www.galaxy.com/data-centers/).

site_name: NSA Utah Data Center (Bluffdale / Camp Williams)
load_basis: Design continuous power requirement reported in 2013 press ('constantly using 65 megawatts'); the actual operating load is not public and no later figure was found.
notes: Utility: AP (via AJC, 8 Oct 2013) reports 'The utility that powers the data center', Rocky Mountain Power, analysed its system and found the electrical faults were internal to the NSA facility. Lehi City Corporation appears in no source. Contract form not found. Year: the scheduled 1 Oct 2013 opening was stalled by electrical failures; Computerworld (8 Oct 2013) says the NSA planned to start some computers that week. No source confirming the actual start of operations was found, and it may have slipped into 2014, so 2013 is low confidence. County left null: the campus sits on the Salt Lake / Utah county line and the worklist address (Lehi) and the press dateline (Bluffdale) point to different counties; not verified.

site_name: Microsoft Boydton - LVL datacenter, 960 Prison Rd (former Mecklenburg Correctional Center site)
notes: Utility: Virginia SCC Final Order, Case No. PUR-2021-00137 (22 Feb 2022). Dominion's Cloud switching station is 'located on six acres at the former Mecklenburg Correctional Center (960 Prison Road, Boydton, Virginia)', the same address as this permit; the projects are needed 'to provide service to two delivery points requested by Old Dominion Electric Cooperative, on behalf of MEC, for MEC to provide service to one of its customers in Mecklenburg County'; Microsoft intervened and asked for an accelerated in-service date. So MEC is the retail supplier, ODEC the wholesale supplier, and Dominion owns the transmission; Dominion is not the retail utility here. Whether MEC serves Microsoft under a special contract was not found ('retail' = co-op retail service, form unverified). Year: null. The order shows a 115 kV Cloud station already existed at the address by mid-2021 and the generator permit is 2019, but no source gives the first commercial operation date of this specific site (Microsoft's original Boydton campus dates to 2010 per state announcements, but that is a different parcel). Load: no public MW figure; planned MW not published.

site_name: Equinix Dallas Infomart, 1950 N Stemmons Fwy
notes: Our Trinity Valley EC assignment is wrong. Data Center Knowledge (13 Apr 2017) says Equinix, the Infomart's largest tenant, 'has its own power capacity reserved with electric utility Oncor'. Oncor is the wires utility; under Texas retail competition the energy is bought from a retail electric provider that was not identified, so 'retail' here means delivery by Oncor. Year: DCK (11 Jun 2014): 'Equinix has had presence in the Infomart since 2000'. The Infomart building itself is older, and Equinix bought the whole building in 2018, so 2000 is the start of Equinix's data center operations there, not the building's first use. Load: null. The only capacity figure found is for the whole building in 2017, '100 MW of capacity serving the Infomart today' of which 30 MW was landlord-operated (same 2017 article); that is utility capacity for all tenants, not Equinix's operating load, and is not entered as load. Planned MW not published.

site_name: Digital Realty IAD44, Digital Dulles campus, 43704 Efficiency Dr
serving_utility: Virginia Electric & Power Co (Dominion Energy Virginia)
load_basis: Total capacity of the first building shell (IAD44, 12 data halls) per the contractor's 2024 ABC Metro Washington award listing. This is shell design capacity; how much was fitted out, commissioned or drawing load in 2025 was not confirmed.
notes: Our NOVEC assignment is probably wrong, but no utility or commission document was found, so medium. Evidence for Dominion: Bisnow (29 Jul 2022) reports that Dominion Energy's transmission constraints were expected to delay Digital Realty's 'Western Lands campus near Dulles International Airport' (the earlier name for Digital Dulles), and the ABC award listing says the campus includes six utility substations and 'one transmission switching station that will revitalize Dominion Energy's Loudoun County power shortage'. Neither states outright that Dominion rather than NOVEC is the retail supplier. Digital Realty's IAD44 fact sheet (https://go2.digitalrealty.com/rs/087-YZJ-646/images/DS_Digital_Realty_2023_IAD44_Property_factsheet_EN.pdf) names no utility. Year: null. The fact sheet is dated 2023 and the award is in the 2024 program, so the first building was delivered around 2023-2024, but no source gives the commercial operation date; our 2024 guess is plausible and unconfirmed. Planned: Data Center Frontier (2020) reports 96-144 MW per building and 'more than 1 gigawatt' in total (https://datacenterfrontier.com/featured/article/11428827/voices-of-the-industry); 1000 is entered as that lower bound.

site_name: Google Council Bluffs data center (original campus), 1430 Veterans Memorial Pkwy
notes: Utility: Data Center Knowledge (19 Jun 2007) on the original announcement: 'The local utility, MidAmerican Energy'. In April 2014 Google and MidAmerican announced an agreement for MidAmerican to supply Google's Council Bluffs data center with up to 407 MW of wind-sourced energy (https://www.environmentenergyleader.com/stories/googles-iowa-data-center-buys-407-mw-of-recs,28158), a renewable supply arrangement on top of ordinary service; its exact tariff form was not looked up. Year: the same 2007 article quotes Google: 'Right now the plan is to go online in spring 2009'. That is a plan, not a confirmed start, hence medium; Google's own Iowa page only says it has been in Iowa since 2007 (the investment announcement). Our 2008 guess is one year early if the plan held. Load: no public MW figure for this campus; the 407 MW is a wind-supply ceiling for Council Bluffs as a whole, not load, and is not entered. Planned MW not published.

site_name: QTS Chicago, 2800 S Ashland Ave (former Chicago Sun-Times printing plant)
load_basis: Critical power capacity of the first building at full fit-out per trade press (Bisnow, Mar 2018: 'capable of providing 24 megawatt of critical power'). Capacity, not measured load; the status of the second building by 2025 was not confirmed.
notes: Utility: NO acceptable source naming the provider was found, so utility_source_url is null and ComEd is entered only as a territory inference (it is the sole mapped utility), confidence low. QTS's own Chicago page says only that it partners with local utilities; Bisnow (2018) reports QTS building an on-site electrical substation without naming the utility. A directory site's blog mentions ComEd substations feeding the site (lead only, not cited). Year: Converge Digest (16 Jul 2016) reports QTS opened the facility; Commercial Search (7 Jul 2016) reports phase one complete; matches our 2016. Planned: 56 MW for the campus, 24 MW for the first building (https://commercialsearch.com/news/chicago-sun-times-printing-plant-reborn-as-data-center).
